messages:
Alex: quick mindshare — prototyping a sidecarless egress broker for Private customers. tiny managed broker in tenant VPC that forwards to our regional relays. goals: avoid host sidecars, preserve tenant source IPs when requested, keep control plane surface small.
Priya: nice. what responsibilities does the broker take on? NAT, TLS termination, auth, or just forwarding? 🤔
Alex: minimal: TCP/HTTP forwarder, short-lived certs from CP, optional SNAT preservation. no app TLS termination by default. control plane provides routing rules.
Sam: sounds like a slim relay. how is this materially different from current relay agent?
Alex: ownership & scope. relay agent = per-host footprint + feature set. broker = per-tenant small cluster (1-3 replicas per AZ). tenant routes egress to broker. fewer host changes for customers.
Morgan: IP preservation nit: to keep source IPs we either need ENI attachment per broker or proxy-protocol passthrough to a tenant-provided NLB. ENIs scale badly across many tenants.
Devon: failure modes? if the broker fails, fallback must be non-disruptive. CP should be able to flip routes to regional relays or enable SNAT fallback. avoid blackholing.
Anita: auth attack surface: we cant hand long-lived keys. short-lived mTLS certs from CP CA, rotated hourly/daily, and CP tracks revocations and health.
Priya: rollout: some customers require deterministic egress IPs. support a reserved-ip mode backed by ENI or small static pool; but limit to premium tenants.
Sam: propose three offering tiers: shared-snat (cheap), reserved-ip (dedicated ENI/static IP), passthrough (tenant manages NLB and preserves source IP).
Morgan: operational telemetry: broker must emit trace-id, cert metadata, active connections, per-route latency. Console needs to show which broker handled traffic.
Anita: compliance: logs must capture broker id, cert issuer/expiry, and rotation events. if customers want in-VPC TLS inspection, we must document risks and offer an air-gapped/on-prem variant.
Devon: network onboarding pain: broker onboarding should be an IaC module (CloudFormation/Terraform) that applies route table entry + security group changes. automated, minimal permissions.
Alex: rough config example:
```
broker:
  cp_endpoint: https://cp.redwood.internal
  mode: reserved-ip|shared-snat|passthrough
  cert_ttl: 1h
  health_check: /healthz
```
Alex: CP API surfaces needed: register_broker(tenant_id,cidr,mode,desired_ips), broker_status(tenant_id), rotate_cert(tenant_id).
Morgan: add quota enforcement in the broker to protect relays (client-side QPS caps). CP should surface per-tenant quotas.
Priya: autoscaling guidance required — broker sees aggregated traffic so recommend replica counts based on concurrent sockets, egress RPS, and tokenization patterns. include socket backlog tuning.
Sam: perf tradeoff: broker-level batching could reduce cost but may add tail latency. need perf tests vs sidecar batching. Ill help with the spike.
Devon: fallback policy suggestion:
- primary: local broker
- on broker failure: CP flips route to regional relay
- if route flip fails: SNAT via shared egress pool
Must have safe rollback tooling for route flips and staged cutovers.
Anita: offboarding: revoke certs, remove route entries, transition to shared-snat. documented playbook required for orgs with compliance windows.
Priya: multi-AZ: brokers must be deployed AZ-local and we should recommend AZ-affine route rules so traffic stays local. that implies at least 1 broker per AZ, 2 replicas for HA.
Alex: decisions & action items:
- decision: prototype sidecarless egress broker with modes (shared-snat, reserved-ip, passthrough)
- risks: IP allocation cost, single-broker overload, route-update races
- next: Priya + Devon to author IaC + onboarding playbook (EOW)
- next: Morgan to spec trace header propagation + Console representation
- next: Anita to enumerate compliance/audit logging requirements
- Sam to join spike for perf testing
- Alex will draft short RFC after spike results
eng-sre-bot: deploy-bot noticed redeploy of infra-staging at 1701103000 — unrelated.
Alex: thanks all, filing notes here for visibility and follow-up.
